paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you can have every gift in the building and still come up empty if love isn't driving. Paul says tongues without love are only "a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal" (1 Corinthians 13:1). Prophecy, knowledge and mountain-moving faith without love? "I am nothing" (1 Corinthians 13:2). Even giving away everything, he says, "I gain nothing" (1 Corinthians 13:3), so love is not an extra topping, it's the whole dough.

So what does love look like? Paul doesn't leave it fuzzy: "Love is patient, love is kind" (1 Corinthians 13:4). It keeps no account of wrongs, it rejoices in the truth, and it "bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things" (1 Corinthians 13:5-7). Friend, that's a recipe you can actually check yourself against, and I'll be honest, I find a few spots where my own batch needs work. That's okay, because the dough forgives, and love is something you keep practicing.

Paul also says why love wins: the gifts belong to now, when "we know in part" (1 Corinthians 13:9), but love "never fails" (1 Corinthians 13:8). Now we see "a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face" (1 Corinthians 13:12). So don't chase the gifts and forget the heart behind them. "And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love" (1 Corinthians 13:13).
